glossary.upi.simple: A way to send money from one phone to another in seconds.
glossary.upi.example: Ammi pays the vegetable seller by scanning his QR code with UPI.
glossary.upi_pin.simple: Your secret number for sending money. You never need it to receive money.
glossary.upi_pin.example: A buyer says, "Enter your PIN to get my payment." That is a trick.
glossary.collect_request.simple: A UPI message that asks you to pay. Saying yes sends your money out.
glossary.collect_request.example: A stranger sends a collect request named "prize". Decline it.
glossary.otp.simple: A one-time code sent by SMS to check it is really you. Never share it.
glossary.otp.example: A caller says he is from the bank and asks for your OTP. Hang up.
glossary.kyc.simple: Checking who you are, with ID papers, before an account is opened.
glossary.kyc.example: An SMS says "Your KYC ends today, tap this link." That is a common trick.
glossary.scam.simple: A trick to make you hand over money or secret details.
glossary.scam.example: "You won a lottery, just pay a small fee first" is a scam.
glossary.helpline_1930.simple: The national number to report online money fraud. Call it fast.
glossary.helpline_1930.example: Kiran lost money to a fake call. Kiran called 1930 that day and also reported on cybercrime.gov.in.
glossary.inflation.simple: When prices slowly go up over time, so the same money buys less.
glossary.inflation.example: A cup of tea costs more today than when Nani was young.
glossary.budget.simple: A plan for how you will use your money, made before you spend it.
glossary.budget.example: Sana writes down fees, bus fare and snacks at the start of the month.
glossary.interest.simple: Extra money paid for borrowing, on top of the amount borrowed.
glossary.interest.example: Borrow ₹1,000 and pay back ₹1,100: the extra ₹100 is interest.
glossary.emi.simple: A fixed amount paid every month to pay back a loan bit by bit.
glossary.emi.example: A phone bought on EMI means a payment every month until it is paid off.
glossary.loan_app.simple: A phone app that lends money. Some are fake and harass people.
glossary.loan_app.example: A fake loan app wants to see all your contacts and photos before it lends.
news.2026-W41.upi_fraud.headline: The PIN trick: you never pay to get paid
news.2026-W41.upi_fraud.body: Sana is selling her old cycle. A buyer messages: "I sent the money on [[upi]]. Just enter your [[upi_pin]] to receive it." Stop right there. A PIN only ever sends money out. Getting money needs no PIN at all. Another trick is the [[collect_request]]: it looks like money coming in, but saying yes takes money from you. Before you tap, read the screen slowly. Does it say "pay" or "receive"? If someone rushes you, that is a warning sign. A real buyer can wait two minutes.
news.2026-W41.upi_fraud.q: A buyer asks for your UPI PIN so you can "receive" money. What is true?
news.2026-W41.upi_fraud.o1: You need a PIN to receive money
news.2026-W41.upi_fraud.o2: A PIN is only needed to send money
news.2026-W41.upi_fraud.o3: Sharing the PIN once is fine
news.2026-W41.upi_fraud.why: A UPI PIN only sends money out. Receiving money never needs it, so anyone asking for it wants to take money.
news.2026-W41.prices_inflation.headline: Why the same ₹100 gets you less each year
news.2026-W41.prices_inflation.body: Ask Nani what a plate of idli cost when she was young. The answer will be much less than today. That slow rise in prices is called [[inflation]]. It happens in most years, a little at a time, so we hardly notice it. But it means money kept still slowly gets you less. That is why a [[budget]] made last year may not fit this year. Look at your big costs, like bus fare and food, every few months and update your plan. Saving for a goal? Its price may also rise by the time you get there, so leave a little extra room.
news.2026-W41.prices_inflation.q: Bus fare went up but Ravi's budget stayed the same. What happens?
news.2026-W41.prices_inflation.o2: His money goes further than before
news.2026-W41.prices_inflation.o3: Less is left for his other plans
news.2026-W41.prices_inflation.why: When a cost rises and the plan stays the same, the extra comes out of something else. Updating the budget shows this early.
news.2026-W41.interest_family_loans.head: Borrowing from family: kind, but still a loan
news.2026-W41.interest_family_loans.body: When money is short, many of us borrow from an uncle or a neighbour. A family loan often has no [[interest]], or very little, and that kindness is real. But it is still a loan, and an unclear loan can hurt a relationship more than a wallet. So agree on three things: how much, by when, and in how many parts. Paying back a small fixed amount each month works like an [[emi]] and is easier than one big payment. Write it down, even in a notebook, so nobody has to remember. A moneylender may charge a lot of interest, so always ask the total you will repay before you agree.
news.2026-W41.interest_family_loans.q: Your aunt lends you money with no interest. What helps most?
news.2026-W41.interest_family_loans.o1: Agree on how much and when you repay
news.2026-W41.interest_family_loans.o3: Skip it, family loans do not count
news.2026-W41.interest_family_loans.why: Even a kind loan is a promise. A clear amount and date keep both the money and the relationship safe.
news.2026-W41.loan_app_rules.headline: Instant loan apps: read before you tap 'agree'
news.2026-W41.loan_app_rules.body: Ads say you can get money in minutes. Some [[loan_app]] offers are honest, but many fake ones are a [[scam]]. Under India's rules, a real lender must show the full cost, including [[interest]] and fees, before you agree. The loan should come straight to your own account, and the repayment, often an [[emi]], should be clear. No lender is allowed to threaten you or message your family and friends. Warning signs: it wants your contacts and photos, takes a big "fee" first, or has no clear name and address. Talk to a trusted adult before any loan.
news.2026-W41.loan_app_rules.q: Which is a warning sign of a fake loan app?
news.2026-W41.loan_app_rules.o1: It shows the full cost before you agree
news.2026-W41.loan_app_rules.o2: It sends the loan to your own account
news.2026-W41.loan_app_rules.o3: It wants to see all your contacts
news.2026-W41.loan_app_rules.why: Real lenders show the cost and pay into your account. An app that wants your contacts may use them to shame or threaten you.
news.2026-W41.payment_safety.headline: Five seconds that keep your money safe
news.2026-W41.payment_safety.body: Most money tricks work by making you rush. A caller says your [[kyc]] ends today, or your account will be blocked, and asks for the [[otp]] that just came on your phone. Real banks never ask for your OTP, PIN or password on a call. Pause, hang up, and check with a trusted adult. If money is lost to a [[scam]], speed matters: call the [[helpline_1930]] or report on cybercrime.gov.in as soon as you can. Keep screenshots of the messages. Telling someone is nothing to be embarrassed about, and it helps stop the next trick.
news.2026-W41.payment_safety.q: Money just left your account after a fake call. What is the best first step?
news.2026-W41.payment_safety.o1: Wait a week to see if it comes back
news.2026-W41.payment_safety.o2: Call 1930 or report on cybercrime.gov.in fast
news.2026-W41.payment_safety.o3: Share the OTP again to cancel it
news.2026-W41.payment_safety.why: Reporting fast gives the best chance to stop the money. 1930 and cybercrime.gov.in are the official places to report.
